# Nginx security update

## Upgrade instructions

Update the CLI, check the proposed release, then upgrade the stack:

```sh
kvsctl update-cli
kvsctl check
kvsctl upgrade
```

This release needs no `kvsctl` newer than 26.10.4 and introduces no database
migration. The upgrade can recreate PHP-FPM and cron as well, so wait for
active conversions to finish first. Updating the CLI alone does not replace
nginx.

From the installation's Compose directory, check the version nginx reports:

```sh
docker compose exec -T nginx nginx -v
```

It should print `nginx/1.31.9`.

## Nginx 1.31.9

The nginx image moves from 1.31.8 to 1.31.9, released on November 18, 2026
with fixes for ten vulnerabilities. Four of them concern features the
stack's nginx configuration uses, HTTP/2, TLS and the `resolver` directive:

- memory corruption in HTTP/2 flow control, rated major
  ([CVE-2026-123007](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-123007));
- an endless loop of a worker process while reading a request body over
  SSL, rated major
  ([CVE-2026-118899](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118899));
- a use-after-free in HTTP/2 when `worker_connections` are not enough
  ([CVE-2026-123633](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-123633));
- a use-after-free in the resolver when the same name is resolved in
  simultaneous subrequests
  ([CVE-2026-123634](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-123634)).

The other six concern HTTP/3, the mail proxy, the stream module, PROXY
protocol version 2 with dynamic certificates, and `alias` combined with
`try_files` in certain configurations. The complete list is on the
[nginx security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)
page.

Nginx 1.31.9 also rejects request header lines without a colon, and chunked
request bodies whose framing overhead is too large. See the
[nginx changes](https://nginx.org/en/CHANGES) for the other fixes.

Native installations made by `kvs-install.sh` use the nginx.org mainline
packages and receive 1.31.9 from their system package updates; this stack
release does not change them.

## Base images

The publish job checks that every image the stack runs unchanged still
matches its registry tag, and several were rebuilt upstream since 26.11.0.
The image lock is therefore resolved again, with the same tags:

| Image | Version |
| --- | --- |
| PHP-FPM and cron | 8.1.34 with the security backport, 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 |
| MariaDB | 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3 |
| Manticore Search | 29.9.0 |
| memcached | 1.6.45 |
| acme.sh | 3.1.6 |

Only the digests move: these are upstream rebuilds of the same releases.
The FFmpeg and ImageMagick restrictions of 26.11.0 stay in
place, and every PHP-FPM and cron build still runs
`kvs-media-security-check`.
([e507dbd](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/e507dbd))

## kvsctl

`kvsctl` and `kvsctl-release` are built with Go 1.27.4, which fixes
[GO-2026-6859](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6859), a crash of an HTTP/1
server in `net/http` that `govulncheck` reports on the paths the CLI uses
to reach the Docker engine, the release manifest and the registries.
([df7cb98](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/df7cb98))

[Full comparison with 26.11.0](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/compare/26.11.0...26.11.1)
